Each stat shows: - its title (Most Toppled, Most Coveted, Pocket Pick, Old Faithful, Arch-Nemesis, Fallen Hero, The Record, Last Laugh, Springloaded, Survivor: those the stats parts delivered and the player has data for), - the card, as a real card face, - the player's number for it ("taken down 37×", "stolen 6×", "you play it 4× as often as everyone else"), - and **the card plays an in-game animation that fits**, reused from the board's FX (`apps/web/src/fx/`: exits, entrances, the trap reveal, the Allure mark and steal, attack lunges, ...). Examples from the brief: - **Most Toppled**: the card plays its Death animation. - **Most Coveted**: the Allure effect is placed on it, then it is taken. - **Pocket Pick**: the Trap reveal animation. Reuse, don't rebuild: drive the existing FX on a card outside a game board. Where an FX assumes a board (anchors, lanes), give it a small stage on the landing rather than duplicating the effect. New FX only where no existing one fits a stat, and say which in the PR. Behaviour: - Cycles on a named interval (a constant, not a literal); the player can step forward/back and pick a stat directly. - Holds still under reduced motion, under a pointer or focus and while the page is hidden, like the home hand (R639); reduced motion shows the static card and number. - Stats with no data are skipped; with no games at all the floor shows what it shows today for a new player. - The whole floor still fits exactly one screen below the main one, desktop and phone, no further scrolling (the tracker's one exception). - The clear-stats control stays. ## Done when - Component tests cover the cycle, skipping empty stats, the pause conditions and reduced motion; `landing.test.tsx` covers the floor. - A ruling note in this issue's block (or an R639 amendment) states the showcase, with its proving tests. - A screenshot of a few stats mid-animation, on desktop and phone, in the PR. ## Plan _Written by `claude-3` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/39723461640)) before anyone built this.
